title: United States bombs Iranian nuclear sites at Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan
body:
On 22 June 2025 the United States struck three Iranian nuclear sites, joining Israel's air campaign that began on 13 June. President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that the US had completed a very successful attack on the three sites, Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan. Fordow is a deeply buried enrichment facility near Qom, Natanz is Iran's largest enrichment complex, and Isfahan houses conversion and fuel fabrication facilities.

Air Force chief Gen. Dan Caine said 14 bunker-buster bombs were dropped from B-2 stealth bombers on at least two sites, including Fordow, and that more than two dozen Tomahawk missiles launched from a submarine targeted Isfahan. It was the first combat use of the GBU-57 bomb. US officials said 125 aircraft were involved and 75 precision bombs were delivered. Trump said Iran's key nuclear enrichment facilities had been "completely and totally obliterated," which Al Jazeera could not independently verify.

The International Atomic Energy Agency said no increase in off-site radiation levels had been reported. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the attack a grave violation of the UN Charter, international law and the Non-Proliferation Treaty, and Iran said it reserved all options. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the strikes a dangerous escalation. Trump warned that any Iranian retaliation would be met with force far greater than what was witnessed. Iran responded on 23 June with missiles at the Al Udeid air base in Qatar.
